extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and usage rules for writing Reuters news copy, covering spelling, punctuation, usage, capitalization, conversions and sensitive terminology for reporters and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Accountability Office (U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be abbreviated to GAO in headlines or at second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaborone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Gaborone, not Gabarone.

rubrics_metrics.name: gaff, gaffe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gaff is a hook; gaffe is a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: gage, gauge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A gage is a pledge or offer as a guarantee. Gauge is a standard or means of measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: gales
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'gales' rather than 'gale-force winds'. A gale is less powerful than a storm in nautical parlance.

rubrics_metrics.name: gallon
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion rules between Imperial, US gallons and litres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imperial -> litres roughly multiply by 9 and divide by 2; precisely multiply by 4.546. US -> litres roughly multiply by 4; precisely multiply by 3.785. Imperial -> US roughly multiply by 6 and divide by 5; precisely multiply by 1.201. US -> Imperial roughly multiply by 5 and divide by 6; precisely multiply by 0.833.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gambia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not the Gambia, West Africa.

rubrics_metrics.name: gambit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not simply an opening move (in chess or metaphorically) but one that involves a sacrifice or concession. 'Opening gambit' is tautological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gandhi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Gandhi, not Ghandi.

rubrics_metrics.name: gantlet, gauntlet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'gantlet' for the military punishment 'running the gantlet'; 'gauntlet' for an iron glove.

rubrics_metrics.name: gaol
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'jail' instead of 'gaol'.

rubrics_metrics.name: gas
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage vs gasoline and plural forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms: gases, gassing, gassed. The American 'gasoline' means motor fuel; in Europe it's 'petrol'. Do not use 'gas' as a synonym for 'gasoline' — it could cause ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: gay
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Now universally used as a synonym for homosexual. Do not use it in other senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: gearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indicator of a company's ability to service its debt. Explain if used in financial stories, but best avoided. See glossary of financial terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geneva Conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on mentioning gender and avoiding stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use language that perpetuates sexual, racial, religious or other stereotypes. Do not cite a person's gender, race, religion, nationality, sexual orientation or marital status unless relevant to the story; consider where to place such information. Do not assume police, firefighters or soldiers are men. Use same terms for men and women where possible (e.g. 'mayor' not 'mayoress'). Use 'chairman, chairwoman' not 'chair'; 'spokesman, spokeswoman' not 'spokesperson' (note: guidance lists spokesman/woman rather than spokesperson). Do not describe a woman’s dress/hairstyle where you would not describe a man’s.

rubrics_metrics.name: general (military ranks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalisation and hyphenation of military ranks and second reference usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military ranks should never be abbreviated and should be capitalised when referring to a specific individual. Ranks in main English-speaking countries are not hyphenated (e.g. Lieutenant Colonel), but follow local practice for exceptions (e.g. Canada and India hyphenate). At second/subsequent reference, use the surname OR his/her rank (e.g. Brown or the general, not the major general). Ranks in non-English-speaking world should be translated without hyphens. US rank-star explanation: brigadier-general one star, major-general two, lieutenant general three, general four. British army has brigadier not brigadier general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentile
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone not a Jew, or not a Mormon. Capitalise.

rubrics_metrics.name: generation -- first/second
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care: 'first-generation immigrant' can mean either people who have immigrated or the children of immigrants. 'Second-generation' likewise ambiguous — be specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: geriatrics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical care of the elderly. The noun is 'geriatrics', the adjective 'geriatric'. It does not mean just elderly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage distinguishing historical and current terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The united Germany is formally the Federal Republic of Germany. Write 'East Germany' when referring to the former Communist state but 'eastern' or 'western Germany' when referring to parts of the unified Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: German spellings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate an umlaut by adding an 'e' after the inflected vowel, e.g. 'von Weizsaecker' not 'von Weizsacker'; 'Fuehrer' not 'Fuhrer'.

rubrics_metrics.name: get, got
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is always a stronger verb. Find it and use it.

rubrics_metrics.name: ghetto
rubrics_metrics.description: No extended guidance; listed as headword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'ghetto'.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI, GIs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A U.S. soldier (from 'government issue'). Use only in informal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: giant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use when describing companies. In general avoid this adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: gibe, gybe, jibe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A gibe is a taunt or sneer. To gybe is to swing a sail over or alter course. In American style 'gibe' is a taunt and 'jibe' is to swing a sail or to be in accord/agree with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gibraltar, Strait of
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'Straits'. Use 'Strait of Gibraltar'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gipsy / Gypsy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'Gypsy' when referring to the Roma people. See 'Roma'. Do not capitalise when used generically to describe someone constantly on the move.

rubrics_metrics.name: girl
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any female older than 18 is a 'woman' not a 'girl'. Use 'woman' not 'lady'. A male older than 18 is a 'man'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Girl Guides
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Now simply 'Guides'.

rubrics_metrics.name: global
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'global' for things affecting the whole globe (e.g. global warming). Avoid when companies claim a 'global network' unless represented in all business centres; consider using 'world' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMT – Greenwich Mean Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage for time conversions in international stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMT is spelled as the international standard and should be capitalised. Convert a local time into GMT when relevant (e.g. 8:30 a.m. (1330 GMT)). Give conversion when previewing important events or statements. Military uses 'Zulu' for GMT.

rubrics_metrics.name: goalkeeper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word in sports reporting. 'Keeper' may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: go-between
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'go-between'.

rubrics_metrics.name: God
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise when referring to the God of any monotheistic religion. Lower case any pronoun references. Lower case 'gods' and 'goddesses' for polytheistic religions.

rubrics_metrics.name: godchild, goddaughter, godfather, godmother, godparents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case, no hyphen. Similarly with 'godsend' and 'godspeed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Godthaab
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Nuuk, Greenland' instead of Godthaab.

rubrics_metrics.name: going public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term for a privately owned company that seeks a listing on a stock exchange and issues shares to the general public. Also known as a 'flotation' or issuing an 'IPO'.

rubrics_metrics.name: golden share
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A share that confers sufficient voting rights in a company to maintain control and protect it from takeover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden Week
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A series of Japanese national holidays from late April to early May. Write in quotes as '"Golden Week"' in headlines and at first reference in the text and then without the quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: good, bad (markets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid simplistic labels in markets reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For financial and commodity markets, 'good news' and 'bad news' depends on positions in the market. Avoid using them.

rubrics_metrics.name: goodbye
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'goodbye', not 'good bye' or 'goodby'.

rubrics_metrics.name: goodwill
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used as noun and adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: gourmand, gourmet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'gourmand' is a glutton; a 'gourmet' an epicure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gospel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise for a specific reference to the books of the New Testament (the Gospels). Lower case for 'gospel music'.

rubrics_metrics.name: governance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other than 'corporate governance', meaning rules governing companies' affairs, 'governance' is often used to mean simply 'government', which is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: governor-general, governors-general
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note hyphen in the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: graffiti
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scribbling on a wall; plural noun. The singular is 'graffito'.

rubrics_metrics.name: gram
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'gramme'. Use 'kg' for kilogram (no full stop). Convert to ounces for weights up to 400 grams, to pounds for larger weights. Rough conversions: grams to ounces divide by 30 (precisely multiply by 0.035). Grams to pounds roughly multiply by two and divide by 900 (precisely multiply by 0.0022).

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: a, an
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'a' before words that begin with consonant sounds (e.g. a historian, a hotel, a NATO member). Use 'an' before vowel sounds (e.g. an heir, an honour, an OPEC member).

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: adjectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adjectives sparingly. Avoid adjectives that imply a Reuters judgment. When using an adjective and a noun together as an adjective, hyphenate (e.g. a blue-chip share). When using an adjective and the past participle together adjectivally hyphenate (e.g. old-fashioned morality). Do not hyphenate adverb+adjective when the adverb stands alone (e.g. well known), but hyphenate when paired as a new adjective (e.g. well-known artist). Do not hyphenate if the adverb ends in -ly (e.g. poorly planned operation).

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: adverbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement of adverbs with auxiliary verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the adverb between the auxiliary verb and the past participle (e.g. 'France has already refused...' not 'France already has refused').

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: as, like
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'As' compares verbs, 'like' compares nouns. Example: 'He fought as a hero should.' vs 'He acted like a hero.'

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: collective nouns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most collective nouns and names of countries, governments, organisations and companies take singular verbs and singular neuter pronouns (e.g. 'The government... said it'). Exceptions: 'police' (plural), 'the couple' (the couple are), and sports teams (teams take plural verbs and pronouns).

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: neither
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Neither' on its own always takes a singular verb. 'Neither... nor' governs two elements only; if both elements singular use singular verb; if one singular and one plural, the verb agrees with the nearest noun. Prefer 'neither... nor' not 'neither... or'; use 'not... or' not 'not... nor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: participles (unattached)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unattached participles are acceptable where sense is clear, but avoid when they make the sentence absurd or ambiguous. Examples provided of bad usages and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: split infinitive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid splitting infinitives unless the alternative is an unnatural word order.

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: that, which
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'that' in defining clauses (the cup that cheers). Use 'which' in non-defining/informative clauses (the cup, which was blue...). Avoid unnecessary 'that'.

rubrics_metrics.name: grammar: who, whom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Who' is the subject, 'whom' the object. Substitute 'he'/'him' to test which fits; follow common usage and be ready to use 'who' as the object where that sounds natural.

rubrics_metrics.name: granddad, granddaughter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same pattern applies to grandmother, grandfather, grandson.

rubrics_metrics.name: grand jury
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grand jury reviews evidence presented by a prosecutor and determines whether there is probable cause to return an indictment. Under the US Constitution a grand jury indictment is required for federal criminal charges. Only about half of US states use grand juries. See U.S. courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand Prix
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise in the title of a race or event (e.g. Monaco Grand Prix), but lower case generally (e.g. Michael Schumacher won his first grand prix). The plural is 'grands prix'.

rubrics_metrics.name: grand slam
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case when describing tennis tournaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: grass court
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two words as an adjective plus noun (Wimbledon’s grass courts). One word as an adjective: 'grasscourt tournament'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Britain, United Kingdom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great Britain comprises England, Scotland and Wales. The United Kingdom comprises Great Britain and Northern Ireland. In sports reporting use 'Britain'. See United Kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: great-
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate great-grandfather, great-grandmother, great-great-grandson etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: grey / gray
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'grey' (but 'gray' in American style).

rubrics_metrics.name: grisly, grizzly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Grisly' means ghastly; 'grizzly' means grey-haired and is also a bear.

rubrics_metrics.name: gross domestic product
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be expressed as GDP in a headline and at first reference, but copy should spell out the full explanation at second reference. GDP is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country; it does not include income from overseas investments or remittances. Use in preference to GNP. Usually used as GDP growth in percent; often called economic growth but spell out term. GDP per capita may be used to compare countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ground rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules that apply in particular circumstances, not general or basic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: gross national product
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total value of goods and services produced by an economy, including income from overseas investments and remittances from nationals working abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: grow (companies vs farmers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Farmers grow crops. Companies do not 'grow' revenues (avoid 'grow' for company revenues).

rubrics_metrics.name: gruelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cliché best avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: guest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'guest' as a verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gulf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage for Middle East Gulf vs Gulf of Mexico.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'the Gulf' for Middle East Gulf. Do not use 'Arabian' or 'Persian' Gulf. Write 'the Gulf of Mexico' in full at first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: gully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'gully', not 'gulley' (cricket fielding position).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gypsy (see Roma)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use when referring to the Roma people. See Roma. Do not capitalise when used generically.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMT/Time conversions guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When to convert local time to GMT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert local time into GMT when Greenwich time is relevant to the rest of the world or when previewing important events; give conversion in parentheses and use GMT in headline/first references as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Haarlem, Harlem
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Haarlem is in the Netherlands, Harlem in New York City.

rubrics_metrics.name: habeas corpus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writ to produce a prisoner before a court, usually used to establish whether the person's detention is legal. When used in stories, define its meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habsburg
rubrics_metrics.description: Headword listed (no expanded guidance in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Haiti
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not an island. It shares Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: hale, hail
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Hale' = free from disease or to pull/haul. 'Hail' = to salute or call out, or an ice shower. 'Hail a cab.' 'A person is hale and hearty.'

rubrics_metrics.name: half
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note forms: halfhearted, halftrack; half brother, half size; half-baked, half-cocked, half-hour, half-life, half-moon, half-truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: half-mast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate. Military protocol distinguishes 'half-mast' for ships/naval stations and 'half-staff' for other uses on land.

rubrics_metrics.name: haj, haji
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'haj' (not hadj or hajj) for pilgrimage to Mecca; 'haji' is someone who has performed the haj.

rubrics_metrics.name: halftime
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halley's comet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case 'c' in 'comet'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hands off
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate when a compound modifier: 'She adopted a hands-off policy' and keep 'her hands off decisions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamas
rubrics_metrics.description: How to refer to the group and suggested story context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to it as 'the Islamist Hamas movement'. Suggest including background: its leaders have offered a long-term truce in return for a viable Palestinian state; it continues to say it will not formally recognise Israel and its 1988 charter calls for the destruction of the Jewish state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton (Bermuda dateline)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form 'HAMILTON, Bermuda' as a dateline for the Bermudan capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: hang / hung
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person is 'hanged'; a picture is 'hung'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hangar, hanger
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Hangar' is a shelter for aircraft; 'hanger' for clothes.

rubrics_metrics.name: hara-kiri
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hara-kiri' not 'hari-kari'.

rubrics_metrics.name: harass, harassment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'harrass'. (But 'embarrass' is an exception.)

rubrics_metrics.name: hard court / hardcourt
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hardcourt' as one word as an adjective (e.g. hardcourt tournament).

rubrics_metrics.name: hard fought
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid this cliché in sports reporting; most competitive matches are hard-fought and it is a story if they are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: hardline, hardliner
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell as one word, without hyphen.

rubrics_metrics.name: hat-trick
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenated.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-bomb
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hydrogen bomb' in text unless directly quoting someone. 'H-bomb' may be used in headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: head of state
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful — it is not always the prime minister.

rubrics_metrics.name: headroom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: healthcare
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: hedge fund
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A private investment fund in which institutions and individuals may invest, typically aiming for high returns from short-term movements using leveraged positions and strategies such as short selling, swaps, derivatives, program trading and arbitrage.

rubrics_metrics.name: heavenly bodies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise the names of planets, stars and constellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: hectare
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convert to acres roughly multiply by five and divide by two; precisely multiply by 2.471.

rubrics_metrics.name: heights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert heights of mountains, buildings etc. from metres to feet, not yards.

rubrics_metrics.name: hemorrhage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'bleeding'.

rubrics_metrics.name: here (avoid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Here' can lead to confusion and ambiguity; often unnecessary to give a locator in a lead paragraph. Use city dateline or place later in copy where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: heroin
rubrics_metrics.description: Headword listed (no expanded guidance in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: hertz
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A unit of frequency of one cycle per second. It usually requires explanation, e.g. '16,000 hertz (cycles per second)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hezbollah
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Shi'ite Islamist group in Lebanon backed by Syria and Iran. It is a political party with a formidable guerrilla army.

rubrics_metrics.name: HICP
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, a measure of inflation calculated under common rules by all EU member states. In Britain the HICP is known as the CPI, but they are the same index.

rubrics_metrics.name: hi-fi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hi-fi'.

rubrics_metrics.name: high-tech / high-technology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'high-tech' only as adjective. As a noun write 'high-technology'. Not 'hi-tech'.

rubrics_metrics.name: high commission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case except when specific: 'British High Commission'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hike
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'rise' or 'increase' when referring to pay, prices, etc. 'Hike' is jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: hint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'hint' because it risks making a value judgment. Be specific about who said what and where and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: hippie
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'hippy'. A rebel against conventional standards and values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a noun or adjective refers to those whose ethnic origin is in a Spanish-speaking country. Be more specific where possible (e.g. Colombian or Mexican). Note people from Portuguese-speaking countries are not Hispanic. See 'race'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People in Spanish-speaking countries usually include father's family name followed by mother's (sometimes linked by 'y'). Give full name at first reference, but only the father's family name at second reference unless person is normally known by combination. Follow commonly accepted usage for Portuguese/Spanish/Brazilian names and nicknames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispaniola
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Caribbean island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: historic, historical
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'A historic event' = major and dramatic; 'a historical event' = part of history. 'Historic' is nearly always the word needed in Reuters copy but use with care to avoid cliché.

rubrics_metrics.name: hit by
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid usage when meaning affected by.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'hit by' when you mean 'affected by'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hitchhike, hitchhiker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'hitchhike, hitchhiker'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hitler
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First name was Adolf not Adolph. His title was 'Fuehrer' (leader) not 'Fuhrer'.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV / AIDS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'AIDS' is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). 'AIDS' applies to advanced stages of HIV infection. Initials AIDS and HIV may be used at first reference with the full name given lower in the story. Do not write 'HIV virus'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hizbollah
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the 'Hizbollah' spelling. See 'Hezbollah'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hoard, horde
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'hoard' is a hidden stock or treasure; a 'horde' a multitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: hoary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'hoarey'; meaning ancient or white with age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hobson's choice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not the lesser of two evils, but no choice at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: hoi polloi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'the hoi polloi'. Prefer 'the masses' or 'the common people'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holland / Netherlands
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'the Netherlands' except in datelines, where it is just 'Netherlands' (e.g. ARNHEM, Netherlands, May 16 ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: holocaust
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wholesale slaughter or destruction by fire. Capitalise when referring to the Nazi massacre of European Jewry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holy Places
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holy Places of Islam are Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem (in that order). Describe relevant sites and access restrictions; non-believers not allowed in Mecca/Medina. Use full explanation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: homemade, homemaker, homeopathy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: homemade = one word; homemaker = one word; use 'homeopathy' not 'homoeopathy'.

rubrics_metrics.name: home schooling / home-schooled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two words for 'home schooling', but hyphenate 'home-schooled' and 'home-schooler'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hometown
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: homosexual
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to both men and women. Do not write 'homosexuals and lesbians' — instead use 'homosexual men and women' if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: honorifics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See courtesy titles, nobility, religious titles, royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: hoof-and-mouth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'foot-and-mouth' instead of 'hoof-and-mouth'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hopefully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except in quotation, do not use 'hopefully' to mean 'it is hoped that...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hospitalise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'hospitalise' as a verb. Prefer 'taken to hospital' or 'treated in hospital'; often drop the reference because seriously ill people are usually treated in hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: host
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable as a verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: hostile bid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bid for a company that is not supported by its senior management.

rubrics_metrics.name: hot spot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two words. Can mean an area with wireless connectivity, a global trouble spot, or a point of intense heat in a fire.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Commons, the Commons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when referring to a specific body (e.g. the U.K. 'House of Commons').

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Representatives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when referring to a specific body (e.g. the U.S. 'House of Representatives').

rubrics_metrics.name: housing unit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'home' or 'household' instead of 'housing unit'.

rubrics_metrics.name: human being
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Just human' will do in many contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: humorist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'humorist'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hundredweight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UK/U.S. long = 112 pounds / 50.8 kg. U.S. short = 100 pounds / 45.4 kg.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurricanes / cyclone / naming
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most severe storms are cyclones (spiral winds inwards). In the Caribbean and on the US east coast such a storm is called a 'hurricane'. Meteorological offices name tropical storms with human names in alphabetical sequence. Capitalise names once designated (e.g. Hurricane Katrina). Use 'it' as pronoun, not 'he' or 'she'.

rubrics_metrics.name: hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules and principles for hyphen use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a hyphen if omission might lead to ambiguity (e.g. 'three year-old horses' vs 'three-year-old horses'). Hyphens tend to erode over time. Use hyphen to show paired words form a single meaning (e.g. extra-judicial). Do not hyphenate an adjective and noun when they stand alone ('the left wing'). Hyphenate when pairing forms a new adjective ('first-class result'). Hyphenate numbers+nouns when forming adjectives ('six-cylinder car'). Do not hyphenate adverb+adjective when adverb ends in -ly. Hyphenate two adjectives or adjective+participle when together form new adjective ('dark-blue dress', 'well-tailored suit'). Do not hyphenate 'very' + adjective. If second element is capitalised, hyphenate (Transatlantic exception). If 'pre-' or 're-' followed by 'e', hyphenate (pre-empt, re-employ). 'non-' negative prefixes hyphenated when first element 'non-'. Hyphenate paired nouns where original meanings retained (actor-manager); otherwise don't (housekeeper). Hyphenate verb+adverb formed noun when vowel collision occurs (cave-in). Hyphenate titles when first word is a preposition (under-secretary) or when a noun is followed by adjective (attorney-general) — note official U.S. titles not hyphenated (US Attorney General). Hyphenate fractions. Hyphenate secondary compass points (south-southwest) but not main ones (southwest). Hyphenate compound words when omission causes ugly sound/confusion (cross-section). Hyphenate both terms in phrases like 'short- and medium-range missiles'. If a hyphenated figure is converted, make sure conversion uses hyphen too (within a 10-mile (six-km) radius).

rubrics_metrics.name: hydro
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, no hyphen (e.g. hydroelectric).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperthermia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too hot. Think of '-er' as in very.

rubrics_metrics.name: hypothermia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too cold. Think that 'o' rhymes with low.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAEA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Atomic Energy Agency (Vienna). The U.N. nuclear watchdog. See www.iaea.org

rubrics_metrics.name: IATA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Air Transport Association (Geneva). See www.iata.org

rubrics_metrics.name: ibn / ibn usage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'bin' in Arab names to mean 'son of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICAO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Civil Aviation Organisation (Montreal). See www.icao.int

rubrics_metrics.name: ice age
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case 'ice age'.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICBM
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intercontinental ballistic missile with a range of about 3,500 miles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICO / OIC
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisation of the Islamic Conference. Use 'OIC'. See www.oic-cio.org

rubrics_metrics.name: icon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best used only to describe a religious image.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICRC
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Committee of the Red Cross (Geneva). See Red Cross and www.icrc.org

rubrics_metrics.name: ld al-Adha, ld al-Fitr
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Eid al-Adha, Eid al-Fitr.

rubrics_metrics.name: idiosyncrasy, idiosyncrasies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct spelling 'idiosyncrasy, idiosyncrasies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFC
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Finance Corporation, private sector financing arm of the World Bank, based in Washington. See www.ifc.org

rubrics_metrics.name: ill
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate in compounds e.g. ill-mannered, ill-tempered.

rubrics_metrics.name: illegal immigrant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'illegal immigrant' rather than 'illegal alien'.

rubrics_metrics.name: IISS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Institute for Strategic Studies (London).

rubrics_metrics.name: illicit / elicit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Elicit' = to draw forth or evoke. 'Illicit' = not permitted or illegal. Don't confuse the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: illiquid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markets or instruments are 'illiquid' if there is a shortage of buyers or sellers, making it difficult to find a true price. Opposite of 'liquid'.

rubrics_metrics.name: illusion / allusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Allusion' is a reference in passing. 'Illusion' is a false impression or delusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: ILO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Labour Organization (Geneva). See www.ilo.org

rubrics_metrics.name: imam
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case when describing the official who leads devotions in a mosque. Upper case when part of an official title.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMCO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-Governmental Maritime Consultative Organisation (London), succeeded by the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

rubrics_metrics.name: IMF
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Monetary Fund (Washington). Specialised UN agency overseeing international monetary system; provides funds to member countries with balance of payments problems. See www.imf.org

rubrics_metrics.name: immigrate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'immigrate' correctly; see related entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Maritime Organization, the UN specialised agency responsible for maritime safety, preventing pollution from ships and promoting technical co-operation. See www.imo.org

rubrics_metrics.name: impacted by
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'impacted by' — use 'affected by', 'helped by' or 'hurt by'. Similarly avoid 'impacted on'.

rubrics_metrics.name: impassable vs impassible / impassive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Impassable' = passage impossible. 'Impassible/impassive' = insensitive to pain or feeling. Do not confuse them.

rubrics_metrics.name: impeachment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the United States impeachment is the process of bringing an official before a court/tribunal on charges of wrongdoing in an attempt to remove them from office. It is not the same as being convicted or removed from office.

rubrics_metrics.name: imply, infer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A speaker/writer 'implies' by suggesting indirectly; a listener/reader 'infers' by drawing a conclusion from what is said.

rubrics_metrics.name: important
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify to whom something is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: imports from abroad
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tautology; just 'imports' will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: impostor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'impostor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: impresario
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'impresario'.

rubrics_metrics.name: impress
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Impress' is transitive and requires an object (e.g. 'Jim Smith impressed selectors'). The passive 'was impressive/unimpressive' is permissible but weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: in addition to
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often 'and' or 'as well as' or 'besides' will suffice; likewise 'in order to' can become 'to'.

rubrics_metrics.name: in, into
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'In' shows place; 'into' shows movement (e.g. 'He was in the square when the soldiers marched into the town'). 'Into' is one word; 'on to' is two.

rubrics_metrics.name: inadmissible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'inadmissible' correctly in legal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: in connection with / insofar as / inasmuch as
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clearer, more direct phrasing; avoid clumsy constructions like 'in connection with' when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: inch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convert to centimetres roughly multiply by 5 and divide by 2; precisely multiply by 2.54.

rubrics_metrics.name: include, comprise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'include' only when listing some component parts of a whole. If listing all components use 'comprise' (e.g. 'Benelux comprises Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg').

rubrics_metrics.name: incredible, incredulous
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Incredible' = unbelievable; 'incredulous' = sceptical.

rubrics_metrics.name: incur, incurring, incurred
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forms correctly (incur, incurring, incurred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index, indexes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'indexes' as the plural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indians (U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Native American' (capitalised) is preferred, bearing in mind this includes Inuit who are not Indians. 'American Indian' is acceptable. Be specific and give tribe name where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: indicated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best avoided because it implies subjective interpretation by the correspondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: indict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid suggesting someone is judged without trial. Use 'indicted on a charge of robbing', not 'indicted for robbing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: indirect speech
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not retain present indicative in indirect/reported speech — change is->was, are->were, will/shall->would, has/have->had. Exception: lead paragraphs with source at end may keep present to avoid pedantry. Usually unnecessary to follow 'said' with 'that'.

rubrics_metrics.name: indiscriminate, indiscriminately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'indiscriminate' / 'indiscriminately' correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: indispensable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'indispensable' correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indochina
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No longer used: now refer to Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indonesian names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often Indonesians only have one name (e.g. Suharto). Handle references accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: indoor, indoors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Indoor' is the adjective; 'indoors' is the adverb (e.g. 'He stayed indoors').

rubrics_metrics.name: industrial action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'industrial action' if you mean a strike; be specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: in fact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'In fact' can almost always be excised.

rubrics_metrics.name: infant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child up to 12 months old.

rubrics_metrics.name: infer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A listener/reader 'infers' while a speaker/writer 'implies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: inflation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persistent rise in prices caused by excess money chasing too few goods or contraction in supply. Distinguish demand-pull vs cost-push inflation. The inflation rate is often a primary policy target.

rubrics_metrics.name: inimitable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'inimitable' correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: injuries, wounds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wounds are suffered in combat or inflicted by weapons; injuries by accident or criminal attack. Be specific (e.g. 'His right leg was broken' not 'His leg was broken'). Use 'suffered' rather than 'sustained' or 'received'. Avoid 'hospitalise' as a verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: innocent
rubrics_metrics.description: Report a plea or verdict accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report a plea or verdict as it was made in court. If it was 'not guilty', do not report it as 'innocent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: innocuous
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'innocuous' correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: inoculate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'inoculate' correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: in order to
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a prepositional phrase, just 'to' will usually do.

rubrics_metrics.name: inquire, inquiry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'inquire' and 'inquiry' (not 'enquire/enquiry').

rubrics_metrics.name: inpatient
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One word. Not 'enquire/enquiry'.

rubrics_metrics.name: insignia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly a plural noun but can be treated as singular as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: insolvency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'bankruptcy' for usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: install / instal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'install' (not 'instal'). 'Installation' but 'instalment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: instil, instilled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Instil' not 'instill'; 'instillation' but 'instilment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: instinctive, instinctual
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Instinctive' = prompted by instinct; 'instinctual' = belonging to or related to instincts.

rubrics_metrics.name: in spite of
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'despite' instead of 'in spite of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: insure / ensure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Insure' means to guarantee against loss; 'ensure' means to make sure.

rubrics_metrics.name: international community
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unless it clearly refers to global diplomatic opinion; be specific (e.g. 'the United States and its allies', or 'Muslim countries').

rubrics_metrics.name: International Court of Justice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper title of the World Court in The Hague. Use 'World Court' at second reference. The Court settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Criminal Court
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court set up in The Hague under UN auspices to try crimes such as genocide.

rubrics_metrics.name: international date line
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: internecine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Internecine' means deadly or murderous as well as conflict within a group; 'internecine warfare' is tautologous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A global data communications system; World Wide Web is not synonymous with the Internet. Capitalise as a noun ('the Internet'), lower case as an adjective (internet banking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpol
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Interpol' correctly.
